title: PATENT RESEARCH REPORT
abstract: This technical report synthesizes polymerization and synthesis methodologies for High Acrylonitrile Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (NBR) based on a selected portfolio of seven key patents published between 2011 and 2024. High Acrylonitrile NBR is defined by a bound acrylonitrile (ACN) content typically exceeding 30%, which imparts superior oil, fuel, and chemical resistance compared to low or medium ACN counterparts. The patent landscape reveals a strong emphasis on emulsion polymerization techniques, particularly cold emulsion processes conducted at 7°C to 8°C to minimize polymer branching and gel formation. Key formulation trends include the use of advanced redox initiator systems (such as hydroperoxides paired with reducing agents and iron catalysts like FeCl2 or FeSO4) and precise molecular weight control via incremental dosing of chain-transfer agents (e.g., tertiary dodecyl mercaptan). Furthermore, a major process trend centers on post-polymerization coagulation chemistry, where the choice of salt (magnesium chloride vs. calcium chloride), latex pH adjustment, and the incorporation of additives like gelatin are shown to critically influence the polymer's ion index, Mooney scorch, vulcanization kinetics, and mechanical properties. This report provides a comprehensive cross-patent comparison and detailed extraction of experimental recipes to guide future research and development in high-performance NBR synthesis.

patent_details.patent_title: Process for the preparation of nitrile rubbers
patent_details.relevance_to_target: Discloses emulsion polymerization recipes for NBR latices (Latex A, B, C) with varying acrylonitrile content.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: Latex A: 500 g acrylonitrile to 4.37 kg butadiene; Latex B: 815 g acrylonitrile to 4.0 kg butadiene
polymerization_method.emulsifier: Potassium stearate and DNMK (sodium salt of disproportionated rosin acid)
polymerization_method.emulsifier_loading: 0.53 kg of 5.4 wt% potassium stearate solution, 0.440 kg of DNMK
polymerization_method.initiator: Diisopropylbenzene hydroperoxide (DIHP) and sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate (FSS)
polymerization_method.initiator_loading: 6 g DIHP, 139 g FSS aqueous solution
polymerization_method.catalyst_activator: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence.
polymerization_method.chain_transfer_dosage: Initial 18.72 g (Latex A) or 21.85 g (Latex B), with booster additions of 2.34 g or 5.45 g TDM at specific conversions (37% and 59%)
polymerization_method.pressure: Not disclosed in the analyzed patent evidence.
polymerization_method.ph: Latex A: 8.5, Latex B: 8.5, Latex C: 8.6
polymerization_method.conversion: Interrupted at 70% conversion using hydroxylamine sulfate
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Latex added to 43 kg water and 4 kg saturated magnesium sulfate solution
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Washing with deionized water adjusted to pH 11.5-11.8 with KOH (14 g) at 45°C, filtering, and drying at 100°C for 24 hours
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: Mooney viscosity (ML 1+4 @ 100°C) of 60.5 (Latex A), 32.1 (Latex B), and 29.0 (Latex C); bound ACN of 28.1% (Latex A), 33.9% (Latex B), and 27.9% (Latex C)

experimental_evidence: Latex A was prepared using 500 g acrylonitrile, 4.37 kg butadiene, and 18.72 g TDM, yielding 28.1% bound ACN and a Mooney viscosity of 60.5.
Latex B was prepared with a higher initial ACN charge of 815 g and 4.0 kg butadiene, resulting in 33.9% bound ACN and a Mooney viscosity of 32.1.
Polymerization was conducted at 7°C, initiated by DIHP/FSS, and short-stopped at 70% conversion after 7 hours using hydroxylamine sulfate.
Coagulation was achieved using magnesium sulfate, followed by washing at pH 11.5-11.8 and drying to less than 1% residual humidity.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Demonstrates precise control of bound acrylonitrile content and Mooney viscosity through incremental chain-transfer agent (TDM) dosing and low-temperature emulsion polymerization.

Vulcanization was carried out at 160°C under 120 bar pressure for 30 minutes to prepare specimens for mechanical testing.
Hot air aging was performed at 100°C for 48 hours, and corrosion testing was conducted at 70°C and 80% relative humidity.

Compounding was performed in a 1.5 L laboratory mixer using 100 parts by weight of nitrile rubber.

polymerization_method.monomer_ratio: Butadiene: 61.4 parts, Acrylonitrile: 36 parts, HEMA: 2.6 parts
polymerization_method.water_amount: 220 parts by weight (or 2.1 kg total water for autoclave batches)
polymerization_method.initiator: p-Menthane hydroperoxide (Trigonox NT 50) and Rongalit C
polymerization_method.initiator_loading: 0.02 parts Trigonox NT 50, 2.0 g Rongalit C in premix
polymerization_method.catalyst_activator: FeCl2 (0.030 parts, premix containing 0.845 g FeCl2*4H2O) or FeSO4 (0.030 parts, premix containing 0.986 g FeSO4*7H2O) with EDTA
polymerization_method.pressure: Hydrogenation pressure of 50 to 150 bar (if hydrogenated)
polymerization_method.coagulation_conditions: Latex admixed with 50% dispersion of Vulkanox BKF (0.3 wt% on solids) before coagulation
polymerization_method.post_treatment: Coagulated, washed with water (1 to 5 parts per 100 parts rubber), and dried
polymerization_method.raw_polymer_properties: Mooney viscosity (ML 1+4 @ 100C) of 25 to 142 MU, glass transition temperature (Tg) of -23.1C to -25.8C, bound ACN of 35.3% to 36.6%

experimental_evidence: Nitrile rubber H prepared with FeCl2 premix reached 84.2% conversion in 6.5 hours, while rubber G with FeSO4 reached 86.1% in 7.0 hours.
The monomer system comprised 61.4 parts butadiene, 36 parts acrylonitrile, and 2.6 parts HEMA, with 3.0 parts Texapon K-12 emulsifier.
Mooney viscosities of the resulting rubbers ranged from 25 MU (Rubber F) to 142 MU (Rubber C).
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Proves that using FeCl2 instead of FeSO4 in the redox system yields nitrile rubbers with distinct and improved properties.

experimental_evidence: Latex pH was adjusted to 9.5 using 5% KOH (C6) or to 5.8 using 5% HCl (C13) prior to coagulation.
Coagulation with CaCl2 (0.3 to 1.2 wt%) resulted in higher ion indices (up to 96.2) and shorter vulcanization times compared to NaCl coagulation.
Vulcanizates prepared from rubbers with optimized ion indices showed stress values at 30% elongation of up to 10.2 MPa.
methodology_patents.technical_relevance: Demonstrates that adjusting latex pH prior to coagulation and selecting specific divalent salts (CaCl2) optimizes the polymer's ion index, leading to faster vulcanization rates and superior mechanical properties.
